newsitem.title: UK: Scottish & Newcastle profits up 21 percent.
newsitem.headline: Scottish & Newcastle profits up 21 percent.

text.p: Britain's largest brewer, Scottish and Newcastle Plc, on Monday posted a 21 percent rise in its annual profits before tax and exceptional items to 374 million pounds on Monday.
The company said in a statement the rise reflected a surge in sales of food and its key beer brands in the second half of the year to April 27.
"The initiatives that have been taken have led to improving growth trends and this is evident in each of our divisions," chairman Sir Alistair Grant said in a statement.
The results were at the top end of analysts forecast range of between 361 to 380 million pounds ($631.7 million).

The company benefited from the conversion of pub sites into Chef & Brewer pub restaurants and other brands like Irish pub Finnegan's Wake. Food sales rose 11 percent year on year while food sales per outlet were up 13 percent.
The company also benefited from the successful integration of Courage, acquired from Australian brewer Fosters in 1995.

The beer division saw net margins rise to 8.2 percent from 6.8 percent, helped by strong sales of Foster's lager and John Smith's ale and a decision by S&N to take a lead in the industry to resist pressure for lower prices.

Profits from the beer business rose to 177 million in the year up from 121.4 million pounds in 1996. However, profits at the group's leisure division, including Center Parcs, fell some 9.0 million pounds to 76.5 million.

The group said its leisure profits were held back by a strong pound, which strengthened on average by 10 percent against major European currencies, and low levels of consumer confidence in mainland Europe.
